biography.plain_text: Frans Heesen was a Dutch entrepreneur who founded Heesen Yachts in Oss in 1978 after an earlier career in carpentry and industrial plastics. He built the yard around high-performance aluminium vessels, gaining international recognition with Octopussy in 1988. He sold the company in 2008, retired in 2012 and died in 2025.

long_biography.plain_text:
When Frans Heesen acquired an existing Oss boatyard, he chose to preserve its workforce and business rather than repurpose the site. The decision redirected an entrepreneur who had left school, worked as a carpenter and built industrial-plastics companies into specialist shipbuilding. Amigo, the first vessel bearing his name, followed a year later, and aluminium construction became a defining capability.

The choice positioned the yard for its decisive late-1980s test. American client John Staluppi requested a 44-metre vessel capable of more than 50 knots, and Heesen accepted a contract with severe performance penalties. Octopussy exceeded the target and gave the yard its international breakthrough. Heesen expanded the company before selling it in 2008, retired in 2012 and remained closely attached to the shipyard afterward.
